entries.claim: Request smuggling is proven only when a request the attacker never sent appears in the back-end access log, because a timing change, an unusual status, or a connection reset is equally consistent with ordinary proxy behaviour.
steps: Prove the sink reads a file at all BEFORE testing traversal: fetch a file you KNOW exists on the target and confirm real content comes back.
If you cannot get a known-good read, there is no traversal finding to report — the sink is not proven.
Then apply the traversal value and confirm the returned content is from OUTSIDE the intended directory. Content, not status code.
Reject any result where only the status line differs: proxies, error handlers and WAFs produce status differentials with no file ever read.
variation: - **Do two layers disagree about the same bytes?** — front_back: **do** front end filters, back end parses; **observe** a request the front end 'cleared' but the back end acted on.

- **What PROVES it, beyond a status code?** — state: **do** read the state back; **observe** the change visible to a second identity.
escalation: No effect raw? Walk the encoding ladder: raw -> percent-encoded -> double-encoded -> look-alike separators, one rung at a time, never all at once.

Still flat? You have proven the sink is not reachable on this path, which is a RESULT. Record it and move to the next candidate rather than escalating payloads blindly.
